body.statement: For every finite connected \(G\) and every \(2\le K\le R\), \(\mathfrak C_K(G)\ne\varnothing\).
body.justification: This guarantees that the finite design optimization and both exact formulations have an attainable optimum.
body.gap: Connected-partition existence is standard; it is included only to close the optimization domain, not as a novelty claim.
body.consumer: The MILP and dynamic program can report an optimum rather than an infeasibility artifact.
body.proof_tex: Because \(G\) is finite and connected, one may construct a spanning tree \(T_G\) as follows.  Start with any vertex and, while the current vertex set is not all of \(U\), use connectedness to choose an edge having exactly one endpoint in the current set and adjoin that edge and its other endpoint.  Each step adds one vertex and creates no cycle, so the resulting subgraph is a spanning tree.  Since \(2\le K\le R\), delete any \(K-1\) edges of \(T_G\).  Deleting one edge of a tree increases the number of nonempty connected components by exactly one, and hence the remaining forest has exactly \(K\) nonempty components, say \(C_1,\ldots,C_K\).  They are pairwise disjoint and have union \(U\).  Moreover, each \(T_G[C_k]\) is connected, so its supergraph \(G[C_k]\) is connected.  Thus \((C_1,\ldots,C_K)\) satisfies every condition in \(\mathrm{def:connected-partitions}\), proving \(\mathfrak C_K(G)\ne\varnothing\).
